title: Field dressing game
summary: Open the belly without puncturing the stomach or intestines, then cool the carcass fast.

steps: Make sure it’s dead: approach from behind and touch the open eye with a stick. No blink, no movement.
Tag it if the law requires, and put on gloves.
Lay it on its back with the head slightly uphill.
Pinch up the belly skin and make a shallow cut. With two fingers inside guiding the blade edge-up, open the belly from the pelvis to the breastbone without puncturing the stomach or intestines.
Cut around the anus to free it, and tie it off to keep waste off the meat.
Cut the diaphragm away from the ribs, reach up into the chest, and cut the windpipe and gullet as far forward as you can.
Roll the animal onto its side and pull the organs out. Keep the heart and liver if they look healthy.
Drain the cavity and cool the carcass fast: prop it open, get it off the ground and into shade, and skin it in warm weather.

blocks.cap: Seen from above with the animal on its back. The dashed line is the belly cut.

list: Rabbits and squirrels: pinch the back skin, cut a slit, and pull the hide apart toward the head and feet. Open the belly and remove the organs.
Wear gloves with rabbits. If the liver has white spots, throw the whole animal away (tularemia).
Fish: cut from the vent to the gills, pull out the guts, then scale or skin.

blocks.cap: The vent is the small opening on the belly toward the tail.

list: Birds: pluck or skin, then open the body cavity and remove the organs.

blocks.p: Cook all wild game thoroughly. Bear and wild pig must be cooked through to kill trichinella parasites.
